cards.text: Meet Jeremiah, the LORD's prophet. Right before this, the people flat out told God they will not walk in His good way (Jeremiah 6:16). Now the word of the LORD comes to Jeremiah, and this time God tells him exactly where to stand.

cards.question: Where does God tell Jeremiah to stand and proclaim His message?

answers.text: In the gate of the LORD's house
By the banks of the Jordan

cards.text: Every person of Judah coming through those gates to worship the LORD has to walk right past him. That's grabbing the mic at the office front door on Monday morning, and NOBODY is sneaking by.
Jeremiah speaks for the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, and the first thing out of his mouth isn't doom. It's a way back: correct your ways and deeds.

cards.question: God tells the people of Judah to correct their ways and deeds. If they do, what will He let them do?
God warns the people at the temple gate not to trust in deceptive words. What are those words all about?

cards.text: God even spells out the words: 'This is the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD, the temple of the LORD.' That's like telling everybody, "I've got a gym membership, I've got a gym membership, I've got a GYM MEMBERSHIP," while the card is still in the wrapper.

cards.question: God says that really correcting their ways and deeds means acting ___ toward one another.
God tells the people they can keep following other gods, as long as they treat the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow well.

cards.text: Do all that, and God will let them live in this place, in the land He gave their fathers forever and ever. That's the offer on the table, friend.

But God says they keep trusting in those deceptive words, and it gets them nowhere. They steal, murder, commit adultery and perjury, burn incense to Baal, a false god, and follow other gods they have not known.

cards.question: After all that, the people come and stand before God in the house that bears His Name. What do they say being there gives them?

answers.text: Freedom to keep doing all these things
A fresh start once they turn back
Protection for their harvest this year

cards.question: God asks if the house that bears His Name has become a den of ___ in their sight.

cards.text: Then God says, "Yes, I too have seen it," and just like that, the hideout isn't hidden anymore. Much later, Jesus uses these same words, "a den of robbers," in the temple courts (Matthew 21:12-13).
Then God sends them on a little road trip to Shiloh, where He first made a dwelling for His Name. Way back, Israel set up the Tent of Meeting there (Joshua 18:1).

cards.question: God tells the people to go see what He did to Shiloh. Why did He do it?

answers.text: Because an enemy army was too strong
Because the priests stopped burning incense

cards.question: God says He spoke to the people of Judah just one time, and they missed it.
God says He will do to the house they trust in what He did to Shiloh.
God says He will cast the people of Judah out of His presence, just as He cast out all their brothers, the descendants of ___.

cards.text: Ephraim was Joseph's son (Genesis 41:52). And that's where we'll leave it for now, friend, because God isn't done talking at that gate.

findings.problem: Jeremiah 6:16 says only 'But they said, We will not walk in it.' The card says the people 'told God', which names a listener the text doesn't name. It also calls it 'His good way', but the text says 'the good way'.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Most of Jeremiah 7:6 never reaches the baker. No card tells them about no longer shedding innocent blood in this place, or about the call to stop oppressing the foreigner, the fatherless and the widow. Card 9's false statement only touches the second one indirectly. Card 10 then says 'Do all that', which assumes the baker has heard a list they were never given.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: This blank asks for the last word of Jeremiah 7:15 ('Ephraim'). Nothing earlier sets it up, so the baker can't reason it out and has to guess the wording of the line. Ephraim also shows up here for the first time with no word on who he is. Card 20 explains him only after the question. A better card would ask about the meaning, such as God casting Judah out of His presence, or would introduce Ephraim before asking about him.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: The 'story isn't over' line copies the doc's example opening word for word ('And that's where we'll leave it for now'). It also says God 'isn't done talking at that gate'. That describes the setting of the next passage, which this passage's text doesn't show.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: The walkthrough has only a few real jokes (card 3's office mic and card 7's gym membership). Cards 4, 10, 11, 15 and 20 read like a nice dad being pleasant. Lines like 'That's the offer on the table, friend' and 'a little road trip to Shiloh' are mild. They don't get the laugh-out-loud reactions, disbelief or self-deprecation the character calls for.

rule.text: Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. ... If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
